lines.text: What if Germany had won the First World War? In the spring of 1918, it nearly did.
lines.say: What if Germany had won the First World War? In the spring of nineteen eighteen, it nearly did.

lines.text: Russia had just surrendered. At Brest-Litovsk, Germany took Finland, the Baltics, Poland, Belarus and Ukraine: a third of Russia's people, and nine tenths of its coal.
lines.say: Russia had just surrendered. At Brest-Litovsk, Germany took Finland, the Baltics, Poland, Belarus and Ukraine. A third of Russia's people, and nine tenths of its coal.
cap: and nine tenths of its coal

lines.text: Fifty divisions moved west. By June, German troops were 56 kilometres from Paris, and a giant gun was shelling the city from 120 kilometres away.
lines.say: Fifty divisions moved west. By June, German troops were fifty-six kilometres from Paris, and a giant gun was shelling the city from a hundred and twenty kilometres away.

lines.text: Berlin's plan was written in 1914: Belgium becomes a vassal, Luxembourg is annexed, France loses its iron mines and pays until it can't rearm.
lines.say: Berlin's plan was written in nineteen fourteen. Belgium becomes a vassal. Luxembourg is annexed. France loses its iron mines, and pays until it can't rearm.
cap: and pays until it can't rearm

lines.text: And the whole continent joins one economic bloc, run from Berlin. They called it Mitteleuropa.
lines.say: And the whole continent joins one economic bloc, run from Berlin. They called it Mittel-Europa.

lines.text: Then it all collapsed in a hundred days. What would have changed if it hadn't? Take a guess.
No Treaty of Versailles. No humiliated Germany. And, many historians argue, no Hitler.
